title: COMET: Codebook-based Online-adaptive Multi-scale Embedding for Time-series Anomaly Detection
claim: A unified system trains a quantized codebook on normal data, then adapts it online at inference to score anomalies robustly.
layout: 4 panels: training and inference on top, two detail zoom-ins below; left-to-right flow
description: A four-panel architecture diagram. The top-left dashed blue Training box shows a normal series entering Multi-scale Patching, an Encoder, Vector Quantization and a Decoder. A LOSS box links the input to the reconstructed series. Quantized outputs feed a Coreset scatter plot, which feeds a gray Memory Bank labeled Local Scaling NN Search. The top-right dashed red Inference box mirrors this path for a test series. It adds an Online Codebook Adaptation block with Normal Filtering and Contrastive learning, linked by red dashed Grad arrows. Memory Score and Quantization Score are added to give the Anomaly Score. The bottom row zooms into Vector Quantization, with embeddings mapped to a patch codebook, and into Online Codebook Adaptation: normal filtering, contrastive learning with MSE+SupCon, and index-wise coreset update. Blue, green and yellow color-code the patch scales, and the eye lands first on the colored blocks.
caption: Overall architecture of COMET. (Top-left) During training, input time series are processed via Multi-scale Patch Encoder to capture temporal contexts at different resolutions. The resulting embeddings are mapped to a Vector-Quantized Coreset, where activated codebook entries are stored in the memory bank. (Top-right) During inference, Online Codebook Adaptation selectively updates the codebook by identifying reliable normal samples through pseudo-labeling and contrastive learning. Anomaly scores are computed by combining memory distance and quantization error. (Bottom-left) Detailed illustration of vector quantization, where continuous patch embeddings are assigned to their nearest codebook entries and represented by the corresponding quantized embeddings. (Bottom-right) Detailed illustration of Online Codebook Adaptation, comprising normal filtering, contrastive learning, and index-wise coreset update. Reliable normal samples are selected based on training-activated codebook entries, and the corresponding codebook prototypes are updated to adapt to distribution shifts while reducing contamination from anomalous patterns.
abstract: Multivariate time-series anomaly detection aims to identify abnormal temporal patterns in complex real-world systems. However, robust unsupervised time-series anomaly detection remains challenging because anomalies can manifest over different temporal ranges and emerge from interactions among variables, while distribution shifts can cause normal patterns to drift over time. To address these challenges, we propose Codebook-based Online-adaptive Multi-scale Embedding for Time-series anomaly detection (COMET), a unified framework with three tightly coupled components. First, Multi-scale Patch Encoder learns correlation-aware patch embeddings by combining variable-specific temporal dynamics with shared inter-variable structure across multiple patch scales. Second, Vector-Quantized Coreset quantizes these embeddings into representative normal prototypes, which are used to detect anomalies through a dual score combining quantization error and density-aware memory distance. Third, Online Codebook Adaptation leverages the same codebook structure to identify reliable normal samples from training-activated codebook entries, and then updates the prototypes through contrastive learning at inference time. Experiments on five benchmark datasets demonstrate that COMET achieves the best performance on 39 out of 45 evaluation metrics compared to seven baselines, showing robust performance across diverse evaluation protocols.
